subject: Decision Making
title: Base Rate Neglect
description: A quick win: understand Base Rate Neglect.

hook.text: A test is 99% accurate. You test positive for a rare disease. Most people think there is a 99% chance they are sick.

buildup.text: If the disease affects 1 in 10,000, even with 99% accuracy, most positives are false. The base rate dominates.

discovery.text: Base rate neglect means we focus on the specific information and ignore the background probability.

twist.text: Base Rate Neglect shows that the best decision is often not the most intuitive one.

climax.text: Always ask: how common is this in the general population? The answer changes everything about what the data means.

punchline.text: 99% accurate test, rare disease. Most positives are still false.

quiz.question: Why do people misinterpret 99% accurate test results?
options: They ignore the base rate—how rare the disease is in the general population
